entry.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
entry.summary: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

entry.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
entry.summary: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture. Its construction uses six three-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^6$, specified by a small table. We classify all its tiling complements and spectra: there are exactly 512 complements and 64 spectra, with one translation class of each. Every spectrum has normalized Wiener norm $15/8$. An appendix proves that Goyal's related construction is affinely inequivalent but has the same tiling complements and spectra. The construction and both classifications are proved from first principles. We also give elementary proofs of the positive assertion in dimensions at most seven and for all tile sizes other than sixteen in dimension eight. The remaining case uses our previously established theorem based on the classification of perfect binary codes of length fifteen.
entry.arxiv:comment: 28 pages, 3 tables, no figures; includes a comparison appendix and ancillary Python verification scripts and data

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in a finite abelian group says that a nonempty subset tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral, meaning that the space of complex-valued functions on the subset has an orthogonal basis consisting of restrictions of group characters. We prove the conjecture in the eight-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. In fact, every spectral set and every tile in this space has a tiling complement which is a linear subspace. We first prove that the Fourier support of a nonempty proper subset of density different from one half contains a two-dimensional subspace. Consequently, every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This gives a simpler proof of Kadowaki's dimension-seven result, replacing his use of the classification of Hadamard matrices of order 32 by the classical five classes of order 16. Our dimension-eight proof uses exact finite verifications involving Hadamard matrices of order 32 and perfect codes of length 15. We include the proofs of the reductions used from Kadowaki's preprint, so that neither positive result depends on his dimension-seven theorem. Finally, we give an elementary spectral example of density one eighth in dimension nine whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. Thus, the Fourier-support argument at quarter density does not extend in this form to eighth density. Dimension nine is the only case still unresolved over the field with two elements, and this obstruction shows why the present Fourier-support method cannot resolve it as it stands.
entry.arxiv:comment: 22 pages. Programs, data, certificates, and verification logs are included as ancillary files. Standalone treatment of selected results from the preliminary preprint arXiv:2610.30712, with a new, simpler dimension-seven proof

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

entry.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
entry.summary: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
entry.summary: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral. For the converse implication, we use the Smith normal form of the Walsh matrix to exclude every spectral subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^7$, and of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$, whose size is not a power of two. The sizes $16$ and $32$ are reduced, by a projection argument, to the tiling of point sets attached to binary log-Hadamard matrices of small rank. Using the published classifications of Hadamard matrices of orders $16$ and $32$, we find that exactly sixteen order-$32$ classes up to transposition have dephased binary rank at most seven, and we give explicit tilings for both orientations of each.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages; computational certificates, verification code, and Lean certificate sources included as ancillary files

entry.title: Fuglede--Kadison Determinants of Shifted Matrix Semicircles
entry.summary: We prove a variational formula for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of a self-adjoint matrix semicircle $S_a = a \otimes 1 + \sum_j A_j \otimes s_j$ with deterministic mean $a$. For every real $z$, $\log Δ(S_a - z) = -1/2 + \inf_b F_z(b)$, where the infimum is over positive definite matrices $b$ such that the map $X \mapsto bXb - \sum_j A_j X A_j$ is positive semidefinite, and $F_z$ is an explicit geodesically convex function. Both sides equal $-\infty$ exactly when $z$ is an atom of the spectral measure. The formula was proposed, without proof, in a recent post of Speicher. In the centered case $a=0$ it gives a new proof of the Mai-Speicher capacity formula, and by hermitization it yields a finite-dimensional variational formula for the logarithmic potential of the Brown measure of an arbitrary matrix-valued semicircular element. The proof identifies the determinant with the value of the Dyson action at its critical point and rewrites this critical-point problem as a saddle problem in three matrix variables. For a spectral parameter $z + i\varepsilon$ in the upper half-plane, eliminating two of the variables gives a geodesically convex minimization whose global minimizer is the positive factor $b_\varepsilon$ in a symmetric unitary factorization of the matrix Cauchy transform. The formula on the real axis follows by letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ in the optimal values, with no compactness assumption on the minimizers. At points where the boundary value of the Cauchy transform is nondegenerate, the scales $b_\varepsilon$ converge and the infimum is attained at their limit; this minimizer lies on the boundary of the feasible set when $z$ is in the support of the spectral measure and in its interior when $z$ is in the resolvent set.

entry.title: Weak Tiling by Unions of Non-overlapping Unit Cubes
entry.summary: We study weak tiling by finite unions of pairwise non-overlapping unit cubes in $\mathbb R^d$ that are not necessarily axis-parallel. We obtain a weak-tiling analogue of Keller's classical theorem, which gives a structural restriction on the support of any weak tiling measure associated with the unit cube. This allows us to derive geometric restrictions on configurations of cubes whose union admits a weak tiling. As an application, we prove Fuglede's conjecture for unions of three non-overlapping unit squares in $\mathbb R^2$ as well as unions of two non-overlapping axis-parallel unit cubes in any dimension.

entry.title: Fuglede's Conjecture for Cyclic Groups of Square-free Order
entry.summary: We prove Fuglede's conjecture for finite cyclic groups of square-free order. Specifically, if \(N\) is square-free and \(A\subseteq \mathbb Z_N\) is nonempty with \(|A|=m\), then \(A\) is spectral if and only if it tiles \(\mathbb Z_N\); moreover, these conditions hold precisely when \(m\mid N\) and \(A\) is a complete set of representatives modulo \(m\). This gives a complete structural description of spectral and tiling sets in \(\mathbb Z_N\). The key new ingredient is a prime-coordinate elimination theorem: if \(P\nmid nm\) is an odd prime, then every \(m\)-point spectral pair in \(\mathbb Z_n\times\mathbb Z_P\) projects injectively to a spectral pair in \(\mathbb Z_n\). Its proof combines character-matrix orthogonality, cyclotomic coefficient comparison, and a \(P\)-adic divisibility argument for associated Gram matrices. Iterating this reduction yields the result for arbitrary square-free \(N\), with no restriction on the number or relative sizes of its prime factors.

entry.title: Fuglede's Conjecture on Cyclic Groups of Square-Free Order: The Case of Rapidly Growing Prime Factors
entry.summary: The main result of the paper is that an inductive argument is established to prove the Fuglede's conjecture for an infinite sequence of square-free order cyclic groups. The tile-to-spectral direction of the conjecture holds for all square-free cyclic groups, whereas we prove the spectral-tiling direction only for those groups among them whose prime factors grow rapidly. To achieve this, we develop an inductive technique with roots in a previous paper by the author co-authored with Fallon, Kiss, and Mayeli. Following recent preprints, Fuglede's conjecture remains open only for finite cyclic groups, and until now, there was no cyclic group for which the conjecture was known that possessed an arbitrary number of distinct divisors.

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds for three intervals
entry.summary: We prove that every bounded measurable subset of the real line that is both spectral and a union of three intervals tiles the line by translations, thereby completing Fuglede's conjecture for this class. The proof develops a new cofactor-rigidity method based on the secular determinant of an associated self-adjoint derivative.

entry.title: Rational Spectra for Finite Hadamard Pairs and Bounded Spectral Sets on the real line
entry.summary: We prove that every finite spectral pair \((A,Γ)\) with \(A\subset\mathbb Z\), \(Γ\subset\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), and \(0\inΓ\) has a rational spectrum, that is, \(Γ\subset\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). Our argument relies on a modulus rigidity theorem for generalizedVandermonde systems satisfying inverse-orthogonality relations, constructed by hyperbolic positive-definite kernels. Combined with Galois conjugation and Kronecker's theorem, this rigidity forces the associated exponential nodes to be roots of unity. As an application, using the periodicity and fiberization of one-dimensional spectra, we show that every spectrum \(Λ\) of a bounded measurable spectral set \(Ω\subset\mathbb R\) with \(|Ω|=1\) and \(0\inΛ\) is contained in \(\mathbb Q\). This rational-spectrum result completes a chain of equivalences proven by Dutkay and Lai, which reduces the full one-dimensional Fuglede's conjecture to its finite cyclic analogues over \(\mathbb{Z}_n\).

entry.title: Putnam-Fuglede commutativity and the range-kernel orthogonality of an elementary operator
entry.summary: Given Hilbert space commuting operators $T, S \in \mcl(H)$, such that $T$ is $w$-hyponormal with $\ker T \subseteq \ker T^*$ and $S$ is normal operator. Let $φ_{T, S} \in \mcl(\mcl(H))$ be the elementary operator defined by $φ_{T, S} (X) = T X S^*-S X T^*$. In this paper, we show firstly that (1) $\ker φ_{T, S} \subset \ker φ_{T^*, S^*}$. (2) The range of $φ_{T, S}$ is orthogonal to the kernel of $φ_{T, S}$ ( $ \mcr(φ_{T, S}) \perp \ker φ_{T, S} $ ) if and only if $\ker T \cap \ker S=\{0\}$. Secondly, we will extend these results to the elementary operator $Φ\in \mcl(\mcl(H))$ defined by $\;Φ(X)=A X D-C X B$ where $[A, C]=[B, D]= 0$. Related orthogonality results for the elementary operator $Φ$ are also given.

entry.title: Both directions of Fuglede's conjecture fail in dimension two
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture asserts that a measurable set of positive and finite measure is spectral if and only if it tiles Euclidean space by translations. Counterexamples are known in every dimension $d\ge3$, whereas the one- and two-dimensional cases have remained unresolved. We construct two explicit $60$-point subsets of the rank-two finite Abelian group $\Z_{60}\times\Z_{12}$: one is a translational tile with no spectrum, and the other is spectral but does not tile. A finite-to-infinite transference principle lifts them to bounded subsets of $\R^2$ that are finite unions of unit squares. Consequently, both implications in Fuglede's conjecture fail in dimension two.

entry.title: Sharp stability of Alexandrov's theorem for $C^1$ domains in the small-excess regime
entry.summary: We prove a sharp quantitative stability result for Alexandrov's theorem in arbitrary dimension for bounded $C^1$ open sets in a small-excess regime. More precisely, if $E\subset \mathbb R^n$ is a bounded $C^1$ open set with the same volume as the unit ball $B$, small excess, and scalar distributional mean curvature $\mathcal H_{\partial E}\in L^2(\partial E)$, then, up to a translation, $$ \operatorname{Exc}(E)+|EΔB|^2+|μ-(n-1)|^2 \le C(n)\|\mathcal H_{\partial E}-μ\|_{L^2(\partial E)}^2 \qquad \forall\,μ\in \mathbb R. $$ In other words, both the excess and the symmetric difference from the ball are controlled by the optimal $L^2$-oscillation of the mean curvature. This yields a sharp stability estimate in a genuinely non-parametric regime. The proof combines a $BV$ version of Fuglede's spectral-gap argument, a star-shaped rearrangement for sets of finite perimeter, quantitative estimates for the part of the boundary contained in the tentacles, and a polyhedral approximation argument for the non-graphical region. We note that the $C^1$ regularity assumption enters only as a qualitative technical ingredient of the proof, but all constants in the final estimate depend only on the dimension.

entry.title: Crossed-Product von Neumann Algebras for Incompressible Navier--Stokes Flows and Spectral Complexity Indicators
entry.summary: We introduce a traceable operator-algebraic framework for incompressible transport on M= T3 (and, more generally, compact Riemannian manifolds endowed with a smooth invariant probability measure). Given an autonomous divergence-free velocity field u, the time-1 map $Φ$ induces the Koopman unitary U on L2(M) and the crossed-product finite von Neumann algebra Mu\,:= L$\infty$(M) ___$α$ Z= W$\star$(L$\infty$(M),U), equipped with its canonical faithful normal trace $τ$u. Within Mu we define tracial complexity functionals from commutators [U,Mf] (with Mf the multiplication operators) and associated positive elements, and we connect these quantities to Fuglede--Kadison determinants and entropy-like tracial functionals. In parallel, we introduce bounded regularized advection operators T(s) u\,:= KsTuKs as differential-level probes of transport oncommutativity, and we recall the Lie-bracket commutator identity at the formal generator level. This provides a natural algebraic setting in which tracial invariants are well posed and, in principle, computable on discretizations (e.g. cavity flow and vortex benchmarks).

entry.title: Spectrality of product-form self-similar measures and tiles
entry.summary: This paper studies the Fourier properties of self-similar measures and tiles generated by digit sets of product-form. Let $0 <ρ<1$ be a real number and let $D$ be the direct sum of two consecutive integer sets: $$D=\{0,1,\cdots,N-1\}\oplus m\{0,1,\cdots, L-1\},$$ where $N, m, L \in \mathbb{N}^{*}$ with %$N, L \geq 2$ $N, L \geq 2$. The pair $(ρ,D)$ determines the self-similar iterated function system (IFS) $ \{φ_d(\cdot)=ρ(\cdot+d)\}_{d \in D}$. Let $μ_{ρ,D}$ and $T$ be the associated self-similar measure and self-similar set, respectively. We first prove that $L^2(μ_{ρ,D})$ admits an exponential orthonormal basis if and only if $ρ^{-1}=p\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $N\mid p$, $L\mid p$ and $N\mid \frac{m}{\gcd(m,p^d)}$, where $$d=\max\left\{i:\gcd\left(\frac{mL}{\gcd(mL,p^i)},L\right)\neq 1,i\in\mathbb{N}\right\}.$$ This result extends a series of previous studies, including the cases where $N,L$ are primes [An-Wang, J. Funct. Anal., 2021] and $N=L$ [Liu-Peng-Wu, J. Math. Anal. Appl., 2019]. Furthermore, in the context of the Fuglede conjecture, we show that when $ρ^{-1} =\#D= NL$, the space $L^2(χ_T dx)$ admits an exponential orthonormal basis if and only if $T$ is a translation tile of $\mathbb{R}$.

entry.title: Duality for Delsarte's extremal problem on locally compact Abelian groups
entry.summary: The Delsarte extremal problem for positive definite functions, originally introduced by Delsarte in coding theory to bound the size of error-correcting codes, has since found applications in diverse areas such as sphere packing, Fuglede's spectral set conjecture, and $1$-avoiding sets. Recent developments have established the existence of extremizers in fairly general settings and identified precise linear programming dual formulations, together with strong duality results, in several important cases including finite groups and $\mathbb{R}^d$. In this paper, we consider a generalized Delsarte problem on locally compact Abelian groups, providing a natural framework for harmonic analysis. We extend both the normalization and the objective functional to encompass a wide range of previously studied cases, while avoiding restrictive topological assumptions common in the literature. Within this general setting, we derive the corresponding dual problem and prove a strong duality theorem, thereby unifying and extending earlier results. Naturally, our proof uses harmonic analysis, but the key is a functional analytic approach which distinguishes our proof from existing methods.

entry.title: Some Plancherel identities for unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R$ in duality
entry.summary: In relation to Fuglede's conjecture, we establish several Plancherel-type identities and demonstrate the surjectivity of the Fourier transform between certain unbounded tiling sets of $\mathbb{R}$ that are in duality. In the terminology commonly used in the context of Fuglede's conjecture, our result states that an open set tiles $\mathbb{R}$ by the finite set $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$ if and only if it admits a spectrum (or, equivalently, a dual pair measure) given by the Lebesgue measure on $\left[-\tfrac{1}{2p}, \tfrac{1}{2p}\right] + \mathbb{Z}$.

entry.title: Central operators on complex Banach lattices
entry.summary: We show that the centre of a Dedekind complete complex Banach lattice is a commutative $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebra in the order unit norm. This implies that the order unit norm and the operator norm coincide. As an application of the latter, a Fuglede--Putnam--Rosenblum-type theorem is established. Under an extra condition on the underlying real Banach lattice, which is satisfied when it is order continuous, a spectral theorem is given for the centre of the complex Banach lattice as a whole and for an individual central operator. The ensuing functional calculus for an individual operator is applied to show that central operators have many spectral properties similar to those of normal operators on complex Hilbert spaces. For example, when the spectrum is countable every element is the sum of an order convergent series of eigenvectors.

entry.title: Lower bounds for mask polynomials with many cyclotomic divisors
entry.summary: Given a nonempty set $A \subset \mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, define the mask polynomial $A(X)=\sum_{a\in A} X^a$. Suppose that there are $s_1,\dots,s_k\in\nn\setminus\{1\}$ such that the cyclotomic polynomials $Φ_{s_1},\dots,Φ_{s_k}$ divide $A(X)$. What is the smallest possible size of $A$? For $k=1$, this was answered by Lam and Leung in 2000. Less is known about the case when $k\geq 2$; in particular, one may ask whether (similarly to the $k=1$ case) the optimal configurations have a simple ``fibered" structure on each scale involved. We prove that this is true in a number of special cases, but false in general, even if further strong structural assumptions are added. Results of this type are expected to have a broad range of applications, including Favard length of product Cantor sets, Fuglede's spectral set conjecture, and the Coven-Meyerowitz conjecture on integer tilings.
entry.arxiv:comment: Minor revisions, update of author information; accepted for publication by Advances in Mathematics

entry.title: Commuting self-adjoint extensions of the partial differential operators on disconnected sets
entry.summary: In connection with the Fuglede conjecture, we study the existence of commuting self-adjoint extensions of the partial differential operators on arbitrary, possibly disconnected domains in $\br^d$, the associated unitary group, the spectral measure and some geometric properties.

entry.title: Geometric implications of weak tiling
entry.summary: The notion of weak tiling played a key role in the proof of Fuglede's spectral set conjecture for convex domains, due to the fact that every spectral set must weakly tile its complement. In this paper, we revisit the notion of weak tiling and establish some geometric properties of sets that weakly tile their complement. If $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a convex polytope, we give a direct and self-contained proof that $A$ must be symmetric and have symmetric facets. If $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of intervals, we give a necessary condition on the lengths of the gaps between the intervals.

entry.title: Spectral properties of unions of intervals and groups of local translations
entry.summary: In connection to the Fuglede conjecture, and to Fuglede's original work \cite{Fug74}, we study one-parameter unitary groups associated to self-adjoint extensions of the differential operator $Df=\frac1{2πi}f'$ on a union of finite intervals. We present a formula for such unitary groups and we use it to discover some geometric properties of such sets in $\br$ which admit orthogonal bases of exponential functions (also called spectral sets).
entry.arxiv:comment: v2 minor correction after the referee's suggestions

entry.title: Entropy and determinants for unitary representations
entry.summary: Ergodic theory includes several notions of entropy for probability-preserving actions of countable groups. These include Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy based on Følner sequences for amenable groups, entropy defined using a random ordering of the group, and Bowen's sofic entropy for sofic groups. In this work we pursue these notions across an analogy between ergodic theory and representation theory. We arrive at new quantities associated to unitary representations of groups and representations of other C*-algebras. Our main results show that these new quantities can often be evaluated as Fuglede--Kadison determinants. The resulting determinantal formulas offer various non-commutative generalizations of Szegő's limit theorem for Toeplitz determinants. They make contact with Arveson's theory of subdiagonal subalgebras, and also with some entropy formulas in the ergodic theory of actions by automorphisms of compact Abelian groups.
